4e3f0cb19b74.description_html:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As a Data Science Intern at Mercor, you’ll join a fast-moving, metrics-driven engineering team whose work shapes decisions across the company. You’ll analyze data that directly affects ranking, hiring efficiency, candidate experience and revenue, work with production datasets from your first week, and ship insights that product and engineering act on.

You’ll start on the analyses and tooling your team has wanted but hasn’t had the hands for, and as needs come up you’ll take deep ownership of them, with a named mentor alongside you. You’ll move quickly while keeping a high bar for analytical rigor, clarity and statistical correctness.

Where You’ll Work

Interns start on a rolling basis, so summer, spring and fall terms all work. About three weeks before your start we’ll match you to one of two teams:

  • Product Data Science. The data science function for the marketplace and talent platform: metrics for matching, ranking and hiring efficiency, event instrumentation and data integrity, experiments on the candidate and customer experience, and scoring models that change who gets surfaced for which role.

  • Applied AI Data Science. The data science function inside the org that delivers human data and evaluations to frontier AI labs: operational analytics for live customer projects, automated quality control that gates what ships, and evaluation science that shows a lab where its model breaks and why.

What You’ll Work On

  • Defining north-star metrics and feature-level KPIs for ranking, interview analytics and payouts

  • Designing A/B tests and quasi-experiments and turning results into product decisions within days

  • Building dashboards and lightweight data models so teams can self-serve insights

  • Instrumenting events with engineers and improving data quality, observability and latency

  • Prototyping models, from baselines to gradient boosting, to improve matching and scoring

  • Evaluating LLM-powered systems through rubric design, human-in-the-loop experiments and guardrail testing

What We’re Looking For

  • Pursuing a degree in a quantitative field, graduating 2027 (potentially 2028)

  • Strong fundamentals in statistics, SQL and Python

  • Experience with experiment design, causal reasoning and data analysis

  • Clear communication with engineers, product managers and leadership

  • Curiosity about LLM evaluation, retrieval, ranking or marketplace dynamics

  • Excited to work in person in San Francisco

  • Nice to have: dbt, dashboarding tools, recommendation or search metrics, LLM and agent evaluation

Why Mercor

  • Impact: your work powers how frontier AI labs train and deploy their models

  • Learning: early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

  • Growth: a high-velocity team where interns ship to production

Compensation and Benefits

  • $10K housing bonus if you live within 0.5 miles of our office during your internship

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals/rideshare

  • Health, dental and vision insurance

  • 401(k) eligibility

4e8fbb775070.title_raw: Flight Software Engineering Intern (Simulation/Hardware-In-The-Loop) - Spring & Summer 2027
4e8fbb775070.description_html:
Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage.

About the Team:  

You'll join a small, fast-moving team building the avionics and flight software for a new flight vehicle program from clean sheet. Everything is actively being built, integrated, and tested on real hardware supporting real tests.

This role will focus on developing simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) infrastructure, combining software development, flight simulation, and hands-on hardware integration.

Small team, big ownership, and we move at speeds the rest of the industry doesn't. 

  Spring-Summer: Around 28 weeks (January - August)

Responsibilities:

Support development of a 6-DOF flight simulation including vehicle dynamics, sensor/actuator models, and engine/plant models to verify flight software in closed loop. Support hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) testing, including integrating flight computers, avionics, sensors, actuators, and cable harnesses. Write simulation and test software primarily in C++, with Python and MATLAB used for modeling and tooling. Troubleshoot and integrate hardware using schematics, pinouts, connectors, and common bench tools. Build tooling that makes simulation and HITL testing fast, repeatable, and data-rich through logging, playback, and automation. Independently own simulation and integration tasks from initial setup through testing and troubleshooting. 

Required Qualifications:

Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. Working proficiency in C++. Strong understanding of physics and dynamics fundamentals, including rigid-body dynamics, classical mechanics, reference frames, and equations of motion. Comfortable working hands-on with hardware, including reading schematics and pinouts, building or terminating cables, and troubleshooting hardware. Comfortable using common bench tools such as a multimeter, oscilloscope, and power supply. Comfortable working in a Linux command-line environment. Demonstrated ability to work effectively on multidisciplinary technical teams. GPA of 3.0 or above.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Working knowledge of MATLAB and/or Python for simulation modeling, analysis, and tooling. Experience with 6-DOF simulation, flight or vehicle dynamics modeling, or software-in-the-loop (SITL). Hardware-in-the-loop (HITL), real-time, or embedded systems experience. GNC coursework or projects involving controls, state estimation, navigation, or flight dynamics. Soldering, connectorization, or wire-harness fabrication experience. Hands-on experience with robotics, UAVs/drones, rocketry, FSAE, CubeSat, or similar technical teams. Previous simulation, GNC, avionics, or flight software internship experience. Currently pursuing a graduate degree (MS or PhD) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field. #LI-Onsite

The hourly rate listed for this internship is intended as a general guideline. Final compensation will be determined based on degree level.

Benefits:

  • Time Off: Interns are eligible for 5 days of sick leave and unpaid time off.
  • Office Perks: Weekly paid office lunches and fully stocked breakrooms.
